headline: Broad Rally Closes Out the Week as Hormuz Tensions Set the Stage
body_html:
Equities finished Friday's session on a firmly constructive note, with 395 of 545 names in our universe advancing against just 146 decliners. Semiconductors led all sectors, surging 3.15%, while Homebuilders and Industrials added 1.58% and 1.24%, respectively. Healthcare was the lone laggard, slipping a fractional 0.01%. The tone heading into the weekend was unmistakably risk-on, even as geopolitical crosscurrents gathered force offshore.

Power-adjacent names dominated the leaderboard. Vicor Corporation topped all movers with an 11.15% advance, followed by Forgent Power Solutions at 8.97% and ON Semiconductor at 8.51%. NetApp and Synaptics each cleared 8.5% and 8%, respectively, while CDW Corp rounded out the top six with a 7.85% gain. On the other side of the ledger, Qualys shed nearly 7%, Kadant fell 6.96%, and SolarEdge dropped 5.63%. Metallurgical coal names Alpha Metallurgical Resources and Warrior Met Coal each retreated 3.82%.

The week ahead arrives with a charged macro backdrop. Diplomacy around the Strait of Hormuz remains unresolved — an Iranian official confirmed no signed agreement is expected from Monday's Oman talks — keeping energy supply routes uncertain. BRICS leaders issued a joint call for restraint in the Middle East, but with the Houthi front widening and fresh reports of shipping attacks in the strait, oil markets face a volatile open. Traders will be watching crude closely for direction cues through the session.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Diplomacy Stalls Ahead of Monday Talks
briefs.body: An Iranian official stated that no signed accord on Hormuz passage is expected from negotiations in Oman set to begin Monday, tempering earlier optimism. Separately, a fresh report of a shipping attack in the strait has revived fears over the security of global oil supply routes, putting energy traders on alert at the week's open.

briefs.headline: Oil Eyes the $100 Level as China Demand Outlook Looms Large
briefs.body: Crude prices have retraced toward triple digits, and analysts point to Chinese demand as the pivotal variable determining whether the move holds. With Hormuz passage still contested and BRICS urging maximum restraint in the Middle East, the supply-side risk premium shows little sign of fading heading into the new trading week.

briefs.headline: Trump Points Finger at Iran Over Saudi Pipeline Attack
briefs.body: President Trump indicated that Iran bears likely responsibility for an attack on a Saudi pipeline, a development that could escalate tensions in an already fragile regional environment. The allegation compounds uncertainty around Middle East energy infrastructure and arrives just as BRICS leaders were calling for diplomatic de-escalation.

briefs.headline: BRICS Summit Closes With Joint Declaration on Middle East
briefs.body: Member nations of the BRICS bloc, including Iran and the UAE, adopted a unified declaration urging maximum restraint in regional conflicts. Chinese President Xi Jinping also used the summit to press for a broader BRICS peace role in the Middle East and to court Indian Prime Minister Modi on the sidelines of the gathering.

briefs.headline: Vicor and Power-Chip Names Surge on Renewed Demand Signals
briefs.body: Vicor Corporation rocketed 11.15% on Friday, leading a cohort of power-semiconductor and infrastructure names sharply higher. Forgent Power Solutions gained 8.97% and ON Semiconductor added 8.51%, suggesting investors are rotating into components tied to data-center power delivery and industrial electrification ahead of anticipated order-cycle updates.

briefs.headline: Oracle Plans Further Workforce Reductions in $700 Million Push
briefs.body: Oracle announced an additional $700 million commitment to job cuts, signaling an accelerated restructuring effort even as enterprise-technology spending broadly stabilizes. The move drew attention across the IT-reseller and enterprise-software space, where CDW Corp — up 7.85% on Friday — may face shifting demand dynamics as a major Oracle channel partner.
